answer: Contribution-weighted routing: each identity’s task volume is capped at the copper value of its verified historical deliveries, so fresh clones start near zero capacity. Every new identity must fund a slow warm-up period that an honest operator amortizes once and a cloner pays per copy, making a sybil farm linearly expensive. Fees paid by clones leave an echo in the ledger, letting the routing layer flag clusters that widen faster than their delivery record. A single pearl of verified output thus outweighs a hundred empty registrations.
